p.src: Presently, when Qin Ming and Huang Xin went outside the stockade gate to look, they saw the troops approaching by two routes arrive at the same moment. One party was led by Song Jiang and Hua Rong, the other by Yan Shun and Wang the Short Tiger, each with more than a hundred and fifty men. Huang Xin ordered the men of the stockade to lower the drawbridge and throw open the gates, welcoming both columns into the town. Song Jiang had already issued strict orders: not a single commoner was to be harmed, nor a single soldier of the stockade injured. He ordered them first to storm the southern stockade and kill every member of Liu Gao's household, old and young alike. Wang the Short Tiger was the first to seize the woman for himself. The underlings loaded all the household goods, gold, silver, valuables, and treasures they found onto carts. All the horses, cattle, and sheep were driven away as well. Hua Rong went home, loaded all his possessions onto carts, and brought away his wife, children, and younger sister. All those among them who were residents of Qingfeng Town were released and sent home. When the heroes had finished making their arrangements, the whole company left Qingfeng Town and returned to the mountain stronghold.

p.src: When all the carts, men, and horses reached the stronghold, Zheng Tianshou welcomed them and led them to meet in the Hall of Righteous Assembly. After Huang Xin had exchanged courtesies with the heroes, he sat below Hua Rong. Song Jiang ordered that quarters be found where Hua Rong's family could rest; and that Liu Gao's wealth be divided as rewards among the underlings. Wang the Short Tiger took the captured woman away and hid her in his own room. Yan Shun then asked, “Where is Liu Gao's wife now?” Wang the Short Tiger replied, “This time she is to become my lady of the stronghold.” Yan Shun said, “You may have her; but call her out first. I have something to say to her.” Song Jiang said, “I was just about to question her myself.” Wang the Short Tiger summoned her before the hall, where the woman wept and begged for mercy. Song Jiang shouted, “You vile woman! Out of kindness I rescued you from the mountain, mindful that you were the honored wife of an imperial official. How could you repay kindness with betrayal? Now that you have been captured today, what defense can you offer?” Yan Shun sprang to his feet and cried, “What is the use of questioning such a wanton woman?” Drawing the saber at his waist, he cut her in two with a single stroke. Seeing the woman slain, Wang the Short Tiger flew into a rage. He snatched up a broad-bladed saber and was about to fight Yan Shun, but Song Jiang and the others rose and restrained him. Song Jiang said, “Yan Shun was right to kill this woman. Brother, consider how I did everything in my power to rescue her from the mountain and reunite her safely with her husband, yet she still turned against me and urged him to kill me. Worthy brother, keeping her at your side would bring you nothing but harm in the end. In time, I, Song Jiang, shall find you a better wife who will satisfy you.” Yan Shun said, “That was precisely my thought, brother. If we did not kill her, she would be of no use, and sooner or later she would surely bring harm upon you.” Persuaded by the others, Wang the Short Tiger fell silent and said no more. Yan Shun shouted for the underlings to clear away the corpse and bloodstains, then ordered a banquet prepared in celebration.

p.src: The next day, Song Jiang and Huang Xin presided over a wedding, while Yan Shun, Wang the Short Tiger, and Zheng Tianshou acted as matchmakers and persuaded Hua Rong to give his younger sister in marriage to Qin Ming. Song Jiang and Yan Shun supplied all the customary gifts. They feasted for several days. Five or seven days after the marriage, an underling who had gathered intelligence came up the mountain and reported, “We have learned that Governor Murong of Qingzhou has sent a memorial to the Central Secretariat, reporting that Hua Rong, Qin Ming, and Huang Xin have rebelled. He intends to raise a great army to suppress them and wipe out Mount Qingfeng.” When the heroes heard this, they conferred together: “This little stronghold is no place to remain for long. If a great army should come and surround us on every side, how could we meet them in battle?” Song Jiang said, “I have a plan, though I do not know whether it will meet with your approval.” At once the heroes all said, “We should like to hear your excellent proposal.” Song Jiang said, “South of here lies a place called Liangshan Marsh. It extends for more than eight hundred li, and within it stand Wanzi City and Liao'er Hollow. Heavenly King Chao has gathered three to five thousand troops there and holds the marsh so securely that government soldiers and thief-catchers dare not even look him in the face. Why do we not muster our men and horses and go there to join them?” Qin Ming said, “If such a place exists, that would be excellent indeed. But without anyone to introduce us, why would they readily accept us?” Song Jiang laughed heartily and told them the whole story: how the birthday gifts of gold and silver had been seized, how Liu Tang had brought him a letter and gold in thanks, and how this had led him to kill Yan Poxi and become a fugitive wandering the rivers and lakes. Qin Ming was overjoyed when he heard this and said, “In that case, elder brother, you are their great benefactor. There is no time to lose. We should prepare and depart at once.” They settled the matter that very day, prepared more than ten carts, and loaded them with their families, gold, silver, valuables, clothing, baggage, and other belongings. Altogether they had some two or three hundred fine horses. Those underlings who did not wish to go were given some silver and allowed to descend the mountain and seek another master; those willing to go were enrolled in the ranks, and together with the soldiers Qin Ming had brought, they numbered between three and five hundred men. Song Jiang ordered them to descend the mountain in three detachments, posing as government troops sent to apprehend the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh. When everything on the mountain had been properly packed and loaded onto the carts, they set fire to the stronghold and burned it to bare ground, then descended the mountain in two columns. Song Jiang and Hua Rong led the first party, with forty or fifty men and thirty to fifty mounted riders escorting five to seven carts bearing the families and their attendants; Qin Ming and Huang Xin led eighty or ninety mounted men and the necessary carts as the second party, while behind them came Yan Shun, Wang the Short Tiger, and Zheng Tianshou with forty or fifty horsemen. One or two hundred men left Mount Qingfeng and took the road toward Liangshan Marsh. Along the road, people saw this great body of troops and horses, and the banners plainly proclaiming them government forces sent to apprehend bandits; therefore no one dared impede them. After traveling for five or seven days, they were far from Qingzhou.

p.src: The two stalwarts ceased fighting and galloped over. Reining up before Song Jiang and Hua Rong, they inclined themselves in the saddle, saluted, and both said, “May we ask the honored name of the Divine-Arrow General?” Hua Rong answered from horseback, “This sworn elder brother of mine is Song Gongming, formerly a clerk of Yuncheng County in Shandong, known as Timely Rain. And I am Hua Rong, commandant of Qingfeng Stockade, known as Little Li Guang.” On hearing this, the two stalwarts planted their halberds, dismounted, and bowed to the ground as though toppling mountains and pillars. “We have long heard your illustrious names,” they said. Song Jiang and Hua Rong hastily dismounted and helped the two men up. “May we first ask your honorable surnames and names?” they said. The man in red said, “My surname is Lü and my given name Fang. My ancestral home is Tanzhou. I have always admired Lü Bu and sought to emulate him, and so I learned to use this painted sky-cleaving halberd. People call me Lü Fang, the Little Marquis of Wen. I came to Shandong to trade medicinal herbs, but lost my capital and could not return home, so for the time being I occupied this Mount Duiying and began raiding wealthy households. Recently this stalwart came and tried to seize my stronghold. I offered to divide the mountain with him, but he refused, and so we have come down each day to fight. Little did I know that destiny had ordained our meeting and that today I would behold your honored faces.” Song Jiang then asked the surname of the stalwart in white. The man replied, “My surname is Guo and my given name Sheng. My ancestral home is Jialing in western Sichuan. While trading in mercury, my boat capsized in a storm on the Yellow River, leaving me unable to return home. In Jialing I originally learned the painted sky-cleaving halberd from Military Inspector Zhang of the local garrison. Later I became highly skilled with it, and people came to call me Guo Sheng, the Rival of Rengui. I heard in the jianghu that a halberd-wielding man had occupied Mount Duiying and was plundering wealthy households, so I came straight here to match my halberd craft against his. We have fought repeatedly for more than ten days without deciding victory or defeat. To encounter you two gentlemen today is unexpected good fortune granted by Heaven.”

p.src: Song Jiang called the tavern keeper over and said, “I have many attendants with me. The two of us will sit inside; ask that customer to give up the large table so my men may sit there and drink.” The tavern keeper replied, “I understand, sir.” Song Jiang and Yan Shun sat down inside. Song Jiang first told the keeper, “Bring wine. Serve my men first in large bowls, three bowls apiece. If you have meat, buy some for them to eat, and then come here to pour our wine.” Seeing that the attendants filled the space beside the wine stove, the keeper went to the customer who looked like a constable and said, “If you please, officer, would you let the attendants of the two gentlemen inside use this large table for a while?” The man took offense at being addressed as an officer and snapped, “First come, first served. Why should I change seats for some gentlemen’s attendants? Your lordship will not move!” Hearing this, Yan Shun said to Song Jiang, “Just look how insolent he is!” Song Jiang said, “Let him be. Why lower yourself to his level?” And he held Yan Shun back. The man turned, looked at Song Jiang and Yan Shun, and sneered. The keeper pleaded humbly once more, “Officer, please help me keep my customers happy. What harm can there be in changing seats?” The man flew into a rage, slapped the table, and cried, “You damned fool! You have no eye for men. Because your lordship is alone, you think you can bully me into changing seats. Even if His Majesty Zhao himself came, your lordship would still damned well refuse to move. Raise your voice again and this great fist of mine will show you no mercy.” The keeper said, “But I never said anything!” The man shouted, “As if a wretch like you would dare say anything!” Yan Shun could bear no more. “Hey, you there! Don’t be so damned overbearing. If you won’t change seats, so be it, but there’s no call to threaten him!” The man sprang up, swung his short staff into his hand, and retorted, “I chose to curse him. What business is it of yours? There are only two men under heaven whom your lordship yields to. All the rest I regard as mud beneath my feet.” Yan Shun lost his temper, seized a bench, and was about to strike him. But Song Jiang, struck by the uncommon boldness of the man’s words, stepped between them and urged, “Now, neither of you make trouble. Let me first ask you: who are those two men under heaven to whom you yield?” The man said, “If I tell you, you’ll be struck dumb with amazement.” Song Jiang said, “I should like to hear the illustrious names of those two heroes.” The man said, “One is Chai Jin, Lord Chai, known as the Little Whirlwind, grandson of Emperor Shizong of Chai’s line, who lives in Henghai Prefecture near Cangzhou.” Song Jiang nodded to himself, then asked, “And who is the other?” The man said, “That one is more remarkable still: Song Gongming, the clerk of Yuncheng County in Shandong, known as the Timely Rain and the Guardian of Justice.” Song Jiang glanced at Yan Shun and smiled secretly. Yan Shun had already put down the bench. The man continued, “Apart from those two, your lordship fears no one—not even the Emperor of the Great Song.” Song Jiang said, “Wait a moment. Let me ask you something. Since you mention those two men, I happen to know them both. Where did you meet them?” The man replied, “Since you know them, I will tell you no lie. Three years ago I stayed at Lord Chai’s manor for more than four months, though I never had the good fortune to meet Song Gongming.” Song Jiang asked, “Would you like to meet the Black Third Son?” The man said, “I am on my way to seek him now.” Song Jiang asked, “Who told you to seek him?” The man replied, “His own younger brother, Song Qing, the Iron Fan, gave me a family letter and told me to find him.”

p.src: When Song Jiang finished reading, he cried out in anguish. Oblivious to everything, he beat his own breast and cursed himself: “Unfilial, rebellious son! I committed a crime, and now my aged father has died while I have been unable to fulfill a son’s duty. How am I any different from a beast?” He began dashing his head against the wall and weeping bitterly. Yan Shun and Shi Yong seized hold of him. Song Jiang wept until he lost consciousness and did not revive for a long while. Yan Shun and Shi Yong urged him, “Brother, please restrain your grief for now.” Song Jiang then told Yan Shun, “It is not that I am coldhearted or faithless. The truth is that my aged father was my sole concern. Now that he is gone, I must hurry home through the night. You brothers must go up the mountain yourselves.” Yan Shun remonstrated, “Brother, since the old master has already passed away, even if you reach home now, you cannot see him again. There are no parents in this world who do not die. Please set your mind at ease for now and lead us brothers there. Afterward, I will accompany you home for the funeral; it will not yet be too late. As the old saying goes, ‘A snake cannot move without a head.’ If you do not go with us, worthy brother, how could they be willing to take us in?” Song Jiang replied, “If I wait until I have escorted you up the mountain, how many days would that cost me? That will never do. I shall simply write a detailed letter explaining everything. Take Shi Yong into the band as well, and let them all go up the mountain together. Had I remained ignorant of this, that would have been the end of it; but now that Heaven has caused me to learn of it, every day seems a year, and the urgency is like fire singeing my brows. I need neither my horse nor a single attendant. I shall hurry home alone through the night.” There was no way Yan Shun and Shi Yong could detain him.

p.src: The nine heroes joined into a single company and, leading three to five hundred men and horses, gradually drew near Liangshan Marsh in search of the main road up the mountain. As the company passed through the reeds, gongs and drums suddenly thundered across the water. When they looked, they saw multicolored banners covering the hills and fields, while two swift boats came rowing out across the marsh. The leading boat carried thirty or fifty lesser bandits, and seated in the middle of its bow was a chief: Lin Chong, the “Panther Head.” The patrol boat behind it likewise carried thirty or fifty lesser bandits, and another chief sat at its bow: Liu Tang, the “Red-Haired Demon.” From the foremost boat, Lin Chong shouted a challenge: “Who are you people? Whose government troops are you? How dare you come to arrest us? We shall kill every one of you and spare not a man, so that you may learn the great name of our Liangshan Marsh!” Hua Rong, Qin Ming, and the others all dismounted and stood on the bank to answer: “We are not government troops. We have here a letter from our elder brother Song Gongming, the ‘Timely Rain’ of Shandong, and have come expressly to join your great stronghold and enter the band.” Hearing this, Lin Chong said, “Since you have a letter from our elder brother Song Gongming, please proceed ahead to Zhu Gui’s tavern. Let us first see the letter, and then we shall invite you to meet us.” Someone on the boat gave a single wave of a green flag, and a small boat rowed out from among the reeds. Three fishermen were aboard. One remained to mind the boat, while the other two came ashore and said, “Generals, all of you follow us.” Out on the water, someone aboard one of the two patrol boats waved a white flag. At the sound of the gong, both patrol boats departed together.

p.src: At the hour of the Dragon on the following day, the strategist Wu the Scholar came in person to Zhu Gui's tavern to welcome the party, and they all exchanged greetings. When the formalities were over, he asked for a full account of what had happened; meanwhile, twenty or thirty large, swift boats had already arrived to fetch them. Wu Yong and Zhu Gui invited the nine heroes aboard, while the elderly and children, the carts, horses, and baggage were likewise loaded onto the various boats, which then headed toward Golden Sands Strand. When they came ashore, a host of heroes followed Chief Chao down the pine-lined path to meet them with a full band of drums and music. With Chao Gai at their head, they greeted the nine heroes and escorted them up through the stronghold gates. Each mounted a horse or took a sedan chair, and they went straight to the Hall of Righteous Assembly, where the two sides exchanged formal courtesies. In the row of armchairs on the left sat Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Lin Chong, Liu Tang, Ruan Xiao'er, Ruan Xiaowu, Ruan Xiaoqi, Du Qian, Song Wan, Zhu Gui, and Bai Sheng. As for Bai Sheng, the “Daylight Rat,” he had escaped from the Jizhou prison several months earlier and joined the band on Mount Liang; Wu the Scholar had sent men to provide the means by which Bai Sheng secured his freedom. In the row of armchairs on the right sat Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Huang Xin, Yan Shun, Wang Ying, Zheng Tianshou, Lü Fang, Guo Sheng, and Shi Yong. They seated themselves in two rows, lit a censer in the middle, and each swore an oath. That day the drums and wind instruments resounded; oxen and horses were slaughtered for a great banquet. Meanwhile, the newly arrived comrades were summoned to pay their respects below the hall and then entertained at a feast with the junior chiefs. Rooms were prepared at the rear of the mountain, and the old folk, children, and dependants were moved there and settled in. At the feast, Qin Ming and Hua Rong praised Song Gongming's many virtues and recounted how he had avenged their wrongs in the fighting at Mount Qingfeng. The chiefs were delighted to hear it. They then told how Lü Fang and Guo Sheng had matched their halberd skills, and how Hua Rong had separated their painted halberds by shooting through the silken tassel with a single arrow. After hearing this, Chao Gai did not believe it, though he answered evasively, “If his shooting is truly so exact, we shall watch him compete with the bow another day.”

Wu Yong and Zhu Gui invited the nine heroes aboard, while the elderly and children, the carts, horses, and baggage were likewise loaded onto the various boats, which then headed toward Golden Sands Strand.
When they came ashore, a host of heroes followed Chief Chao down the pine-lined path to meet them with a full band of drums and music.
With Chao Gai at their head, they greeted the nine heroes and escorted them up through the stronghold gates.
Each mounted a horse or took a sedan chair, and they went straight to the Hall of Righteous Assembly, where the two sides exchanged formal courtesies.

In the row of armchairs on the left sat Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Lin Chong, Liu Tang, Ruan Xiao'er, Ruan Xiaowu, Ruan Xiaoqi, Du Qian, Song Wan, Zhu Gui, and Bai Sheng. As for Bai Sheng, the “Daylight Rat,” he had escaped from the Jizhou prison several months earlier and joined the band on Mount Liang; Wu the Scholar had sent men to provide the means by which Bai Sheng secured his freedom.
In the row of armchairs on the right sat Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Huang Xin, Yan Shun, Wang Ying, Zheng Tianshou, Lü Fang, Guo Sheng, and Shi Yong.
They seated themselves in two rows, lit a censer in the middle, and each swore an oath.
That day the drums and wind instruments resounded; oxen and horses were slaughtered for a great banquet.
Meanwhile, the newly arrived comrades were summoned to pay their respects below the hall and then entertained at a feast with the junior chiefs.
Rooms were prepared at the rear of the mountain, and the old folk, children, and dependants were moved there and settled in.
At the feast, Qin Ming and Hua Rong praised Song Gongming's many virtues and recounted how he had avenged their wrongs in the fighting at Mount Qingfeng. The chiefs were delighted to hear it.
They then told how Lü Fang and Guo Sheng had matched their halberd skills, and how Hua Rong had separated their painted halberds by shooting through the silken tassel with a single arrow.
After hearing this, Chao Gai did not believe it, though he answered evasively, “If his shooting is truly so exact, we shall watch him compete with the bow another day.”

p.src: That day, when the wine had brought them to a pleasant half-drunkenness and several courses had been served, the chiefs all said, “Let us stroll before the mountain for a while, then return to the feast.” The chiefs courteously yielded precedence to one another, descended the steps, and strolled at leisure, delighting in the mountain scenery. When they reached the third gate before the stockade, they heard several ranks of wild geese crying clearly in the sky. Hua Rong thought, “Chao Gai's manner just now showed that he did not believe I had severed the silken cord with an arrow. Why not display some skill here today and let them all see it, so that they will respect and submit to me hereafter?” Looking about, he saw that some among their attendants carried bows and arrows, so Hua Rong asked one of them for a bow. Examining it in his hand, he found it was a slender bow gilded and painted with magpies, exactly to his liking. p.src: The magpie-painted bow curved like the full moon; the feathered arrow burst forth like a shooting star. Strong was the hand that drew it, swift its flight from the string. The geese ranged across the sky like wildfowl stretched upon a rack; the archer loosed his shaft as though extending a limed fowling pole. Its shadow fell from amid the clouds; its cry arose from within the grass. The wild-goose line across the River of Heaven broke in alarm; the brotherhood of heroes rejoiced to be joined more closely.

p.src: Hua Rong's arrow indeed struck the third goose in the line, sending it plummeting straight down the mountainside. Soldiers were hastily ordered to retrieve it, and when they examined the bird, the arrow had pierced it squarely through the head. Chao Gai and all the chiefs were astounded at the sight, and they hailed Hua Rong as the Divine-Armed General. Wu the Scholar praised him, saying, “Never mind comparing the general to Little Li Guang—even Yang Youji could not equal such divine skill. Truly, our stronghold is blessed!” From that time on, not a soul in the Liangshan Marsh failed to admire and respect Hua Rong.

p.src: The chiefs returned to the hall and resumed the feast, then retired separately when evening came. The next day another banquet was prepared in the stronghold, and the order of precedence was settled. Qin Ming should originally have ranked directly above Hua Rong, but because Hua Rong was Qin Ming's elder brother-in-law, the company deferred to him and placed him fifth, immediately below Lin Chong. Qin Ming took the sixth seat, Liu Tang the seventh, and Huang Xin the eighth. Below the three Ruan brothers came Yan Shun, Wang the Short-legged Tiger, Lü Fang, Guo Sheng, Zheng Tianshou, Shi Yong, Du Qian, Song Wan, Zhu Gui, and Bai Sheng—twenty-one chiefs in all. Thus the seating was settled. The celebratory banquet then came to an end. The stronghold built more large boats, houses, carts, and equipment; forged spears, swords, weapons, armor, and helmets; and put its banners, robes, crossbows, bows, and arrows in order, preparing to resist the government forces. Of this there is no need to say more.

p.src: Now Song Jiang, after leaving the village inn, hurried home through the night. At the hour of the Monkey that day, he reached the entrance to his native village and rested for a while at Village Head Zhang's tavern. Village Head Zhang was on very good terms with Song Jiang's family. Seeing that Song Jiang looked unhappy and was secretly shedding tears, Village Head Zhang asked, “You have not been home for a year and a half, Constable. Today, happily, you have returned—why does your honored countenance look so troubled? What grieves you? Your case has fortunately been covered by an amnesty, so surely your sentence has been reduced.” Song Jiang replied, “What you say is quite true, uncle. The official case can wait; it is only that my own aged father has died. How could I not be grieved?” Village Head Zhang laughed aloud. “Constable, are you truly in earnest, or are you joking? Your honored father was drinking here only a short while ago and left less than half an hour back. How can you say such a thing?” Song Jiang said, “Uncle, please do not make sport of your nephew.” He then took out the letter from home and gave it to Village Head Zhang to read. “My brother Song Qing writes here plainly that our father died at the beginning of the first month this year, and that they were waiting especially for me to return for the funeral.” After reading it, Village Head Zhang said, “Pah! How could there be any such thing? Around noon today he was drinking here with Squire Wang from the eastern village before they left. Why would I lie to you?” Hearing this, Song Jiang was filled with doubt and could make no sense of the matter. He pondered for a long while and waited until nightfall; then, taking leave of the village head, he hurried home.

p.src: When he entered the manor gate and looked about, there was not the slightest sign of disturbance. The servants of the manor came to pay their respects when they saw Song Jiang. He immediately asked, “Are my father and Fourth Brother here?” A servant replied, “The old master has strained his eyes watching for your return every day, Constable. Now that you are home, he will be overjoyed. A short while ago he returned from drinking with Village Head Wang of the eastern village at Village Head Zhang's tavern by the village entrance, and he is asleep in the inner room.” Song Jiang was greatly startled. Dropping his short staff, he went straight into the main house, where Song Qing came forward and bowed to his elder brother. Seeing that his brother wore no mourning clothes, Song Jiang flew into a great rage. Pointing at Song Qing, he cursed him: “You disobedient beast! What is the meaning of this? Our father is alive and here in the house, so why did you write that letter to make sport of me? Two or three times you drove me to seek my own death, and every time I wept until I fainted. What an unfilial son you are!”

p.src: Song Qing was about to explain when Old Master Song emerged from behind the screen and called out, “My son, do not be angry. Your brother is not to blame for this. I longed every day to see you once more, so I told Fourth Brother to write only that I had died, knowing that would bring you home quickly. I had also heard it said that many outlaws haunt the region around White Tiger Mountain, and I feared that someone might persuade you to join them in the stronghold, making you a man disloyal to your sovereign and unfilial to your father. That is why I hurriedly sent the letter summoning you home. And when Shi Yong came from Squire Chai’s residence, I had him carry the letter to you. The whole affair was my idea; Fourth Brother had nothing to do with it, so do not resent him. I have only just returned from Village Head Zhang’s inn, where I heard that you had come home.”

p.src: When Song Jiang had heard him out, he bowed his head to the floor before his father, torn between sorrow and joy. Then Song Jiang asked his father, “How does the case stand of late? Now that an amnesty has been proclaimed, my sentence must surely be reduced. Village Head Zhang said as much just now.” Old Master Song replied, “Before your brother Song Qing returned, Zhu Tong and Lei Heng spoke vigorously on your behalf. Afterward, the authorities merely issued a single general warrant for your arrest and never came to trouble us again. The reason I have now summoned you home is that I recently heard the court has installed the Imperial Heir and issued an edict of amnesty. All commoners guilty of serious crimes are to have their sentences reduced by one degree, and the decree has already been circulated everywhere for enforcement. Even if the affair comes to the authorities’ notice, you should receive no more than penal servitude or exile; it will not cost you your life. For now, let matters take their course; later we shall devise another plan.” Song Jiang asked again, “Have Constables Zhu and Lei ever come to the manor?” Song Qing answered, “I heard the other day that both of them had been sent away on assignments. Zhu Tong was dispatched to the Eastern Capital, while no one knows where Lei Heng was sent. The county office has now appointed two new men, both surnamed Zhao, to handle arrests and official business.” Old Master Song said, “My son, you are weary and dusty from your long journey. Go to your room and rest for a while.” The whole household rejoiced, as need not be related.

p.src: Evening gradually fell, and the jade hare rose in the east. At about the first watch, when everyone on the manor had gone to sleep, shouts suddenly erupted at both the front and rear gates. Looking out, they saw torches on every side, encircling the Song family manor completely, while voices cried in unison, “Do not let Song Jiang escape!” Hearing this, the old master cried out again and again that disaster had come. From what now arose, it was destined that upon the banks of a mighty river worthy heroes would gather, and amid the crowded marketplace, loyal hearts and righteous courage would be revealed. How Song Gongming escaped from the manor will be revealed in the next chapter.
